newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand sets incentives for financial co mergers.
newsitem.headline: Thailand sets incentives for financial co mergers.

text.p: The central bank of Thailand said on Wednesday that it would offer a host of incentives to promote mergers among finance and securities companies, including the granting of new bank licences.

"This is latest measure approved by the finance ministry for the government to stabilise and strengthen financial institutions which will face increased competition as the Thai financial system comtinues to be liberalised," Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond told a news conference.
Finance companies would be encouraged either to be absorbed into commercial banks or to merge with each other, he said.
"This policy of encouraging mergers is for strengthening the stability and for raising competitiveness in a liberalised financial sector in the future," Rerngchai added.
The latest incentives follow a massive revamp of the troubled and liquidity-hit domestic finance sector last month by the Thai authorities.

In the shake up, the authorities asked 10 weakened finance companies to boost capital and told financial institutions to increase provisioning for non-performing loans, mainly given to the depresssed property sector.

A central bank statement said that those that merge will be eligible for additional retail banking businesses ranging from the ability to accept pass-book savings deposits at lower rates, do foreign exchange dealing and expansion of branches.
Merged groups that have improved sufficiently their financial and managerial strength could also apply for upgrade into commercial banks, it added.

"To be considered for additional retail banking businesses, the group must have a leader of one or up to three companies with combined net capital of 3.0 billion baht ($115.4 million) and net assets of 30.0 billion baht," the statement said.

To apply for a banking licence, the leader of a group must have net capital of 7.5 billion baht and net assets of 75 billion baht. The new bank must be at least a medium-sized bank with net capital and assets of at least 1.5 billion baht and 150 billion baht respectively.
"The merger must also absorb weaker companies as requested by the Bank of Thailand," it said.
Group leaders of mergers must be companies with a good reputation, proven ability and possess human resources that would ensure merged companies could expand with prudence, the statement said.
Finance companies that merged and needed to rebuild their capital through foreign participation over and above the 25 percent limit allowed by the law would be considered on a case by case basis.

Financial institutions interested in merging could submit their applications to the central from Wednesday onwards and those that wised to apply for a banking licence could submit their applications by the end of the year, the statement said.

The first merger of major financial institutions, with government blessings took place last month, when Thailand's largest, but cash-strapped finance company Finance One Plc merged with medium-sized Thai Danu Bank.
Some Thai finance companies have been hit by liquidity woes amid current high interest rates and saddled with poorly performing loans, especially those lent to the ailing property sector.

The Thai cabinet has approved a proposal by the finance ministry to issue up to 100 billion baht in zero coupon bonds to raise funds to help sick property firms. It has also approved securitisation of property sector debt.
